_comment: Copy to config.json and fill in solana.wsUrl / solana.httpUrl with a Helius key (free tier is enough), plus your Telegram bot token and chat id. Robinhood Chain needs no key. THE SIGNING KEY IS NEVER PUT IN THIS FILE - it is read from the FIRSTFILL_PRIVATE_KEY environment variable only, and a key found here is a startup failure.

roster.notes: EVM side is an EIP-7702 delegated ERC-4337 account (delegate 0xe6cae83bde06e4c305530e199d7217f42808555b); nonce 1, zero balance, so trades arrive via a bundler and match on calldata, never on sender. Volume was on Solana until 2026-09-14, when his first real Robinhood Chain buy landed (tx 0x853010bc..., +298,050.7 TWINE, worth about $848 at the time). sizeUsd is what WE spend copying him, in dollars - it has nothing to do with what he spent.

executor._comment: enabled:false means detect and alert only, exactly as before. paper:true runs every gate - quote, build, router pin, simulation, balance check - against live state and live prices, and signs nothing. PAPER STILL NEEDS THE WALLET FUNDED: the simulation reads real balances, so a dry run from an empty wallet refuses at insufficient-input-balance and proves nothing. --paper on the command line forces paper regardless of this file; there is no flag in the other direction.

snipe._comment: Meteora Dynamic Bonding Curve launch sniper, driven by `npm run snipe`. It is SEPARATE from the copy-trading bot above and does not run with it. The Solana signing key is read from FIRSTFILL_SOLANA_KEY (base58, or a solana-keygen JSON array) and a key placed in this file is a startup failure. Run `npm run snipe -- plan` first and READ THE DERIVED ADDRESSES: they are all PDAs, so a wrong config produces a real-looking pool address that has nothing to do with your token.
snipe._config_comment: The DBC config the launch uses. Supply it and the pool address is derived in advance and the whole transaction is pre-signed, so firing is a socket write. Leave it null and the bot still fires, but it cannot pre-sign and must build at fire time, which is slower. It is usually a constant for a given launchpad - ask whoever is launching.
snipe._quote_comment: What you pay in. Defaults to wrapped SOL. This MUST match the config's quote mint; arming refuses if it does not.
snipe._amount_comment: Raw quote units, as a string. wSOL has 9 decimals, so 250000000 is 0.25 SOL.
snipe._minout_comment: Raw base units below which the swap must fail. THERE IS NO DEFAULT and there will not be one: "0" means you accept any fill at any price, which on a launch is a real choice but has to be yours. Set it deliberately.
snipe._fee_comment: computeUnitLimit is the CU ceiling for the whole transaction; computeUnitPriceMicroLamports is what you bid per CU for block space. THE DEFAULTS BELOW HAVE NOT BEEN MEASURED against a live DBC launch - read the CU actually used from the first fill and tighten them.
snipe._send_comment: Endpoints to fire at. Every one gets the same signed bytes, so duplicates are still a single fill. Falls back to httpUrl when empty.
snipe._url_comment: Default to the solana section above when null. A fast endpoint matters more here than anywhere else in this repo.
